overview: This table sets where fighters appear and which way they face at the start of each mission wave.
description: Per-layout arrays of character spawn positions and rotations that override stage defaults for a mission wave.

Id.simple: The name that connects this set of spawn positions to the layout chosen for a stage and mission wave.
Id.technical: FName import key/row name for FGameDataTableRow_MissionLayout (the export labels it ID, and the asset declares ImportKeyField 'Id'); an unassigned value is NAME_None. It is not chosen directly by gameplay: AGameBattleManager::GetCharacterStartTransform resolves the current map row by StudioBattleLevelRequest_CA0.BattleLevel, indexes MapRow->Id_MissionLayout with the current MissionWave->MissionLayoutIndex, and then resolves that name against MissionLayoutDataTables (DTM+0x9B0). The first table in that array whose FindRow finds the key wins. No direct read of the row's own Id member was found; its role is lookup identity.

Location.simple: Where each fighter appears when the battle starts, in the order the game assigns fighters. The game then adjusts the height to reach the ground.
Location.technical: TArray<FVector>, constructor-default empty; every supplied row nevertheless has exactly six entries. When the layout row is selected for the active map/wave and Layout->Location.IsValidIndex(Index), SetTranslation(Layout->Location[Index]) replaces the translation of the base transform taken from the battle area's pair component (or FTransform::Identity). Pair selects that fallback area array, not a different layout array. Coordinates are world-space Unreal units (centimetres). The result's Z is then always passed through GameBattle_TraceGroundHeight(World, Location, +200, -10000), which returns the nearest qualifying ground hit's ImpactPoint.Z + 1 or the original Z when no hit; X/Y are untouched. Zero-valued exported entries are ordinary data, not a skip sentinel: a valid Index still sets translation to (0,0,0) before the Z trace.

Location[].X.simple: The X part of a fighter's starting position, measured in centimetres in the game world. A larger value moves that starting point farther along this direction.
Location[].X.technical: The double-valued FVector X component (exported as a JSON number). It is consumed only as part of the whole Location[Index] value, via SetTranslation, when a layout row is found and IsValidIndex(Index) passes; the subsequent ground trace leaves X unchanged. The native array defaults empty; all 137 exported rows have six entries, and a zero X is data rather than a skip marker.

Location[].Y.simple: The Y part of a fighter's starting position, measured in centimetres in the game world. A larger value moves that starting point farther along this direction.
Location[].Y.technical: The double-valued FVector Y component (exported as a JSON number). It is consumed only as part of the whole Location[Index] value, via SetTranslation, when a layout row is found and IsValidIndex(Index) passes; the subsequent ground trace leaves Y unchanged. The native array defaults empty; all 137 exported rows have six entries, and a zero Y is data rather than a skip marker.

Location[].Z.simple: The written height of a fighter's starting point, measured in centimetres in the game world. The game replaces it with the ground height when it finds ground.
Location[].Z.technical: The double-valued FVector Z component (exported as a JSON number). It is copied with X/Y by SetTranslation when the layout row and slot are valid, but is then overwritten by GameBattle_TraceGroundHeight(+200/-10000): the final Z is the nearest qualifying ground-hit ImpactPoint.Z + 1, or the original Z if no hit is found. Exported values include negative, zero and elevated heights; zero is not a skip sentinel.

Rotation.simple: Which way each fighter faces when the battle starts, in the order the game assigns fighters. Adjusting to the ground leaves that facing unchanged.
Rotation.technical: TArray<FRotator>, constructor-default empty; every supplied row nevertheless has exactly six entries. If Layout->Rotation.IsValidIndex(Index), Result.SetRotation(FQuat(Layout->Rotation[Index])) replaces the rotation of the area-component transform (or identity); Pair does not choose a separate rotation array. FRotator angles are degrees (exported Pitch/Roll are all 0.0; Yaw ranges -180 to 290). Unlike Location, the ground trace only changes translation Z, so within this function the row's rotation is final; a missing row or out-of-range slot keeps the battle-area or identity rotation. All-zero exported rotations are real identity values, not skip markers.

Rotation[].Pitch.simple: How far a fighter's starting pose tilts forward or backward, in degrees. Every current layout keeps the fighter level.
Rotation[].Pitch.technical: The double-valued FRotator Pitch component (exported as a JSON number). It is converted with FQuat and applied through SetRotation only when the layout row and Rotation.IsValidIndex(Index) pass. All 822 exported rotation entries have Pitch 0.0; that is an identity value, not a sentinel meaning 'no override'.

Rotation[].Roll.simple: How far a fighter's starting pose tilts sideways, in degrees. Every current layout keeps the fighter upright.
Rotation[].Roll.technical: The double-valued FRotator Roll component (exported as a JSON number). It is converted with FQuat and applied through SetRotation only when the layout row and Rotation.IsValidIndex(Index) pass. All 822 exported rotation entries have Roll 0.0; that is an identity value, not a sentinel meaning 'no override'.

Rotation[].Yaw.simple: The direction a fighter faces at the start of battle, measured in degrees around the stage. A different value faces the fighter another way.
Rotation[].Yaw.technical: The double-valued FRotator Yaw component (exported as a JSON number). It is converted with FQuat and applied through SetRotation when the layout row and Rotation.IsValidIndex(Index) pass; the ground trace does not alter it. Exported values range -180 to 290 degrees, so -180 and 180 are equivalent facings rather than distinct sentinels.

notes: The supplied export is one asset/shard named MissionLayoutDataTable: 137 rows, RowStruct Class'GameDataTableRow_MissionLayout' from /Script/AbramsDataTable, ImportKeyField 'Id'. Every exported ID equals its row name and every row has six Location and six Rotation entries.

StartInitialLoading registers the name 'MissionLayoutDataTable' under FPrimaryAssetType 'DataTable', whose scan directory is /Game/DataTables; after load completion Tick resolves it through the asset manager and appends the UDataTable to MissionLayoutDataTables (DTM+0x9B0). No other direct reference to that cache or asset name appears in the reconstructed Source.

The only direct source-side consumer chain is MissionWave.MissionLayoutIndex -> Map.Id_MissionLayout[] -> MissionLayout row -> AGameBattleManager::GetCharacterStartTransform. The supplied MapDataTable has 30 rows with 16-element Id_MissionLayout arrays; 134 of the 137 layout row names are referenced at least once, while MAP16_ST112_2, MAP16_ST112_3 and MAP16_ST112_4 are unreferenced. MissionWaveDataTable has 1774 rows: 133 use the -1 no-override sentinel, and all non-negative exported indices (0..4 and 8..13) fall within the 16-element Map arrays.

Precedence is FTransform::Identity -> battle-area pair component transform -> layout Location/Rotation (only when the wave, map row, wave index and character slot all pass their guards) -> final Z ground trace. Native defaults are NAME_None and empty arrays; exported zero locations and zero rotations are ordinary values, not skip markers.

AGameBattleArea::GetCharacterStartTransform (retail 0x1015c60) is a separate area-slot helper used by domain-expansion sub-state 6 and does not consult this table. It should not be confused with AGameBattleManager::GetCharacterStartTransform (0x1015dc0), which owns the mission-layout override.

The C++ path is reconstructed: source comments identify retail RVA 0x1015dc0 and status/verdicts.json currently records a MATCH claim for that RVA from Tools/verify/LANES/w23-deps-1.md. No retail Blueprint graph dump or live retail run was available, so this is not a claim about every possible retail or Blueprint use.

usages.detail: StartInitialLoading registers 'MissionLayoutDataTable'; after load completion Tick resolves its loader and appends the UDataTable to MissionLayoutDataTables (DTM+0x9B0).

GetCharacterStartTransform joins the current mission wave to the active Map row by StudioBattleLevelRequest_CA0.BattleLevel, then indexes Map.Id_MissionLayout[Wave.MissionLayoutIndex] and resolves that name in MissionLayoutDataTables.
When the row and character slot Index are valid, Location[Index] overrides translation and Rotation[Index] overrides rotation before the final Z ground trace.
EGameBattlePair selects the fallback per-pair area component array; an invalid pair or slot leaves FTransform::Identity. The mission layout arrays are not pair-specific.
GameBattle_TraceGroundHeight provides the final Z from a +200/-10000 cm line trace (ground-hit Z+1, otherwise the original Z); layout X/Y and rotation are unchanged.
System360->MissionWave is MissionWaves[RetryCount] for Arcade (and likewise PvE at line 797 and Story at line 820); it supplies MissionLayoutIndex for the join.

Built characters receive ApplyCharacterSetup(Entry.Setup), which consumes Setup.StartTransform for actual placement.
ApplyCharacterSetup sets the character's location/rotation from Setup.StartTransform and caches it as AGameCharacter.StartTransform.
After the intro, Free battle resets the character to the cached StartTransform.
Domain-expansion sub-state 6 uses the separate AGameBattleArea::GetCharacterStartTransform helper; it bypasses the mission-layout join.
